title: Phase 3: ECONOMY - Complete Research with Web Sources
description: Weeks 9-14 - Functional economy system. Research compiled from web sources with detailed implementation.

web_definition.what_is: Goods (or Trade Goods) represent natural resources, manufactured goods, or services which make up the economy. Each good has a base cost that varies in each market depending on supply and demand.
web_definition.what_exists: Victoria 3 has 4 main categories: Staple (food, wood), Industrial (iron, coal, rubber), Luxury (silk, tea), Military (small arms). Over 30 unique goods.
web_definition.how_to_use: Goods are consumed by pops for needs and by buildings for production. Each good has base price, traded quantity, prestige factor, and convoy cost multiplier.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Goods flow through markets. Supply = production + imports. Demand = pops consumption + building input + exports. Price = base × (demand/supply)^elasticity, clamped at 75% ±.
web_definition.how_to_expand: New goods can be added via game files. Each good defines: base_cost, traded_quantity, prestige_factor, consumption_tax_cost

staple.description: Basic consumer goods for population survival and basic comfort

industrial.description: Raw materials and intermediate goods used for production

luxury.description: High-value goods for wealthy populations and status

military.description: Weapons and equipment for military operations

price_formula.victoria_3: price = Base Price × [1 + 0.75 × clamp((BUY − SELL) / min(BUY, SELL), ±1)]
price_formula.constraints: Price varies from 25% to 175% of base price (75% below to 75% above)

web_definition.what_is: Buildings are the primary basis of a country's economy. They employ pops and produce goods. Each building is located in a state and employs pops from that state.
web_definition.what_exists: Victoria 3 has 40+ building types across categories: Rural (farms, mines), Urban (factories), Infrastructure (railways, ports), Government (administrations, military), Development.
web_definition.how_to_use: Buildings convert input goods to output goods. They require pops, goods, and infrastructure. Can be expanded for economy of scale (+1% throughput per level).
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Each building has: building_group, icon, city_type, production_method_groups, required_construction. Buildings auto-expand based on urbanization (every 50 urban = 1 urban center).
web_definition.how_to_expand: New buildings defined in common/buildings with building_group, production_method_groups. Each level adds workforce and production capacity.

key_building_properties.owner: Can be state, private investor, or company
key_building_properties.level: Each level adds capacity and workforce
key_building_properties.economy_of_scale: +1% throughput per building level in same state (first 50 levels)
key_building_properties.throughput: Measures efficiency of converting input to output

construction_sector.description: Produces construction capacity for building new buildings
construction_sector.input_goods: Wood, Fabric (basic) → Iron, Steel, Glass, Explosives (advanced)

trade_center.tariffs: Can be set per good to protect or encourage trade

web_definition.what_is: Construction represents a country's ability to build new buildings. Costs are applied over time as part of national budget, not as lump-sum.
web_definition.what_exists: Each country has base +10 construction capacity + more from Construction Sector buildings. Queue holds projects, capacity allocated weekly.
web_definition.how_to_use: Projects enter queue, capacity allocated by priority. Advanced methods require advanced goods (steel, glass). Government vs private construction split based on Economic System.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Construction Sector uses pops and goods to produce construction capacity. Goods usage scales with actual need, not maximum capacity.
web_definition.how_to_expand: Build more Construction Sectors. Upgrade production methods for faster construction. Use decrees for construction efficiency.

construction_capacity.construction_sector_levels: Each level adds capacity based on production method

costs.labor: Paid from national budget for government construction
costs.private: Goods from investment pool, labor from budget

construction_queue.active_projects: Building projects currently being worked on

implementation_guide.allocate_capacity: distribute capacity to projects in priority order

web_definition.what_is: Production methods represent a building's mode of operation. They determine inputs, outputs, workforce, and effects. Multiple mutually exclusive methods per building.
web_definition.what_exists: Each building has multiple production method groups. Methods unlocked by technology, laws, or other methods. Examples: Simple Farming → Fertilizers → Chemical Fertilizers.
web_definition.how_to_use: Player selects production method per building. Affects: input goods, output goods, workforce type/count, building modifiers, state modifiers.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Production methods have requirements (tech, laws). If requirements lost, auto-switch to first valid method. Methods can unlock advanced methods.
web_definition.how_to_expand: Define in common/production_methods with building_modifiers, state_modifiers, country_modifiers.

web_definition.what_is: Each market has its own prices based on total buy and sell orders. Markets are collections of states with economic connections.
web_definition.what_exists: Every country has a national market. Adjacent markets can trade. World market enables global trade via Trade Centers.
web_definition.how_to_use: Price = base × (demand/supply) with clamping. Local prices affected by market access. High SoL states have higher local prices.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: States with full market access use market price. Isolated states use higher prices (less supply). MAPI = Market Access Price Impact.
web_definition.how_to_expand: Customs unions create shared markets. Trade routes connect markets.

price_factors.demand: Pop needs + Building requirements + Government demand

local_price.importance: Producers in low-access states may lose money

market_access.determines: How connected state is to market

web_definition.what_is: Trade routes allow import/export between markets. Old system: manual routes. New system (1.5+): World Market with Trade Centers.
web_definition.what_exists: Countries can establish trade routes with strategic region partners. Requires convoys for overseas. Trade Centers enable autonomous world market trade.
web_definition.how_to_use: Create route → choose good → set amount → goods flow. Tariffs apply. Trade generates revenue for Trade Centers.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Trade Centers provide trade capacity. Tariffs control flow. Convoys required for overseas.
web_definition.how_to_expand: Build more Trade Centers for capacity. Upgrade ports for convoys. Set tariffs per good.

world_market.world_market_price: Based on global exports vs imports

trade_advantage.definition: How dominant a country is in trading a specific good

web_definition.what_is: Treasury manages national finances: income (taxes, tariffs, fines) and expenses (buildings, military, subsidies).
web_definition.what_exists: Income from: taxation (land, income, production, tariffs), trade revenue, building revenue. Expenses: construction, army, bureaucracy, subsidies, debt interest.
web_definition.how_to_use: Budget shows all income/expense lines. Player can adjust tax rates. Debt accumulates if expenses > income.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Net income = all income - all expenses. Positive = surplus to reserves. Negative = deficit (reserves or debt).
web_definition.how_to_expand: Adjust tax rates per law. Build profit-generating buildings. Manage trade tariffs.
